text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- Parliament amended the Constitution yesterday to make referendum requirements more onerous and to widen the realm of issues not subject to referenda.

- Young Democrat parliamentary group leader Jozsef Szajer said yesterday that the coalition's planned amendment to the electoral law would hamper cooperation between the Young Democrats and the Democratic Forum.
- Sandor Toth of Rozsnyo, Slovakia has been fired for issuing bilingual school reports to his students at the end of the school year.
- Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz of Poland arrives in Budapest today to hold talks with his Hungarian counterpart Gyula Horn.
- Hungary's GDP grew by 1.2% in the first quarter compared to January-March 1996.

- "No sane person likes to pay taxes, especially if they are Hungarian," Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said in the opening speech of yesterday's celebration marking the 10th anniversary of the founding of the tax authority APEH.

- A member of the National Radio and Television Board (ORTT) yesterday attacked the board's decision in awarding two concessions to broadcast on terrestrial television channels, saying subjective considerations prevailed.

- The State Capital Markets Supervision is accusing the brokerage Hoffmann Schneider Securities Kft. (HSS) of accepting and carrying out orders for stock exchange transactions of a manipulative nature.
- The Kanizsai and Kobanyai breweries merged yesterday to create Dreher Sorgyarak Rt.
- Leaders of the Free Democrat party are considering whether to remain in the governing coalition in light of recent snubs by the Socialists.

- Magyar Hirlap says Hungarian ministries are squabbling amongst themselves rather than preparing for variant verdicts on the Danube hydropower project that could be handed down by the International Court of Justice.
- Employees and compensated persons will be favored in the upcoming privatization of the photo processing company Forte Rt.
- The state railways MAV Rt. transported 1.42% more goods in the first six months than in January-June of last year.
